problem: The projection of the intersection between the hyperbolic cylinder $2(x+6)^{2}-5{y}^{2}=10$ and the plane $z=5$ onto the $xy$-plane is a hyperbola. What are the lengths of the semi-axes of the hyperbola?

examples.problem: What is the trace in the $yz$-plane of the elliptic cylinder $\dfrac {x^2} 2 +  \dfrac {(y-2)^2}4  = 1?$
examples.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $yz$-plane, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the cylinder, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{0}^{2}}{2}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ (y-2)^{2} & =4 \\ y-2 & =\pm 2 \\ y & =2\pm 2 \\ y & =0,4\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of two lines $y=0$ and $y=4$ in the $yz$-plane.

feedback.problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the parabolic cylinder $(x-1)^{2}=3y?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The full expression describing all points on our parabolic cylinder is

$$
(x-1)^{2}=3y,\,z=k
$$

where $k\in R$ can vary arbitrarily. 

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:(x-1)^{2}=3y}.
$$

This is an upward-opening parabola with a vertex at $(1,0).$

submitted_fields.submitted_value: An upward-opening parabola with a vertex at $(1,0)$
